title: Workspace, navigation and shared controls
summary: Current shell, workspace dashboard, global discovery, shared input behavior and foreground refresh. Domain-specific editors and permissions are documented in their own areas.

cases.title: Clear drafts on session change
preconditions: The actor is signed into an active approved account and has access to the relevant project.
steps: Change the authentication session epoch.
expected: Registered issue, comment, upload, planning, field, bulk, board and saved-search drafts clear.
notes: The umbrella scenario encloses the complete native UI matrix in one recorded step: issue, comment and selected-file drafts, planning retry intent, custom-field input, bulk retry intent, board layout edits and saved-search retry intent. Each draft is first restored through ordinary navigation to prove registration; then visible sign out/sign in changes the account within the same SPA document. Native search/navigation reopens the scope, previous private intent is absent and actual service readbacks are unchanged. A partial family run does not claim the umbrella expectation.

cases.title: Clear issue drafts on same-SPA account switch
preconditions: The first approved account has a registered unsaved issue draft in a supported editor.
A different approved account can access the underlying project after signing in.
steps: Use the visible Sign out action, then sign in as the other account without reloading the SPA.
Reopen the same issue editor or scope.
expected: The previous account issue draft is not restored into the new session; only current persisted data and new-session selections are shown.
notes: Atomic account-switch boundary for the issue draft family; UC-SHL-0073 remains the umbrella expectation for all eight families.

cases.title: Release destroyed bulk editor ownership after a late response
preconditions: The signed-in writer has a same-tab retained native bulk draft after explicitly confirming navigation away.
The first bulk field write was accepted by the real service; its reply is held while the original bulk component has been destroyed and the clean Backlog route is active.
steps: Deliver the accepted bulk reply after the original component is destroyed.
Use the visible Issues link to leave the clean Backlog route in the same signed-in tab.
expected: The late completion does not re-register the destroyed bulk editor as active dirty work: the clean Backlog route leaves successfully without an unrelated draft confirmation.
notes: The browser fixture holds the actual accepted server reply and uses ordinary links and the native leave confirmation. No Angular internals or fabricated server responses are used.

This atomic case covers dirty-ownership release only. Same-tab draft restoration and exact accepted-item replay remain independently required by UC-SHL-0072 and UC-ISS-0165; they are not inferred from this case.
